title: The Operational Facilitator's alignment finding is a precondition for the tokenholder vote, so alignment review outranks the majority
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 requires that "within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment," announcing the finding on the forum either way — with reasoning attached when the finding is misalignment, and with an added confirmation "that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize" when it is alignment.

A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 then makes the sequencing explicit: "where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Keel Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll."

This is a hard ordering, not a recommendation. KEEL holders never get to vote on a proposal the Facilitator has ruled misaligned, so tokenholder majority is not the top authority in Keel governance — conformity to the Sky Core Atlas is, and one named role adjudicates it. The vote decides only among proposals that have already passed a constitutional filter.

The checks on that considerable power are procedural and reputational rather than structural: a deadline (7 days), a duty to publish, and a duty to give reasons for a rejection. A feasibility confirmation is bundled in as well, which quietly means the Facilitator can also decline to advance something Operational GovOps could not actually execute.

The trade-off is a familiar one: the design prefers the risk of a captured or mistaken reviewer over the risk of a tokenholder majority voting Keel out of alignment with Sky.
